title: LP2 red initials: corrected page-order test
question: Do the pages bearing large red initials have unusual spacing compared with a uniform 13-of-58 page placement?
reader_question: Once pages with ordinary red text are removed, is the pattern of pages with large red initials unusually spaced?
summary: The corrected 13-page list has ordinary spacing under four specified measures; one compressed-bit measure has almost no resolving power at this length.

family.title: Order of visual page markers
family.question: Does a precisely identified visual marker occur on pages in an unusual order?

variant.label: Large-red-initial page presence; uniform placement null

scope.representation: Binary page presence from the archived JPEG image audit: at least one red component of 10000 full-resolution-equivalent pixels, measured with four-connectivity after half-resolution sampling. The original JPEG SHA-256 values are recorded per row in the audit CSV.
scope.procedure: Compare 13 corrected page positions with uniform 13-page subsets of 58; test internal-gap variance in both directions and packed-bit compression with 100000 seeded samples; count span and adjacent-run tails exactly; run evenly spaced and consecutive planted controls.
scope.parameters: Pages 00–57; 13 selected; random.Random(3301) with 100000 subsets; zlib level 9; plus-one Monte Carlo tails; five tail directions with Bonferroni correction.
scope.exclusions: Initial-rune identities, multiple initials on one page, red centroids, nonuniform authorship or section-placement models, alternate image segmentation, arbitrary encodings and any complete decryption rule.

finding: No declared spacing measure is unusual for a uniform 13-of-58 subset. The internal-gap variance is 12.85 (upper-tail estimate 0.328); the longest run is two (exact upper-tail 0.968); the span is 57 (exact lower-tail 1). The zlib score is 16 bytes, matched by 99977 of 100000 random subsets. These are narrow page-order results, not a proof against hidden information.
limitations: Exploratory after source misclassification was noticed. Uniform page placement is only a reference, not an authorship model. The presence bit discards the two second initials and the locations of later initials. Compression has almost no discrimination here; a spaced control also uses 16 bytes. None of these statistics tests a general code.
next_steps: Annotate each large initial and its within-page position before rerunning identity and centroid analyses; test new placement models only with fixed rules and matching controls.

reproduction.environment: Python 3.12 standard library for page-order analysis and independent checker. To regenerate the image-audit CSV, download original-images.zip and install Pillow 11.3.0, NumPy 2.5.4 and opencv-python-headless 5.0.0.93. No network or hosted AI is used during replay.

review.reviewer: Image-derived list cross-checked against the source; exact span/adjacency counts and a second independent Monte Carlo stream

sources.label: Source Round 22 illustration experiment at pinned revision

visuals.caption: Fifty-eight page positions: the published total-red rule, the corrected large-initial set, and two planted controls. LP2-07 and LP2-53 contain only small red text.

reader_note: The corrected large-initial pages have ordinary spacing under the tested uniform-page reference. This does not test the rune identities or rule out other ways the artwork might carry information.
reader_limit: Two pages in the earlier 15-page list contain only small red text. The page-order test has narrow bounds, and its compression measure has little power on a 58-bit string.
scope_summary: LP2-00–57 · 13 pages with large red initials · five page-order tails · 100000 sampled controls and exact span/run counts.
